summary.intent: Debug a failed staging deployment after merging release PR #298, then investigate and fix slow IPNS publish (30s+) and broken token refresh discovered during smoke testing on staging.
summary.outcome: Three PRs created and merged: #308 (Dockerfile stale COPY fix), #307 (release-please title pattern fix + manual v0.25.1 tag), and #309 (full web API client consolidation eliminating duplicate orval generation). IPNS publish made fire-and-forget; token refresh unified across all HTTP paths.

repo: Staging deployment uses a manual 'Tag Staging Release' GitHub Actions workflow that requires explicit invocation with a version input — it does NOT auto-trigger on release tags.
release-please-config.json `pull-request-title-pattern` was missing `${component}`, causing release-please to abort with 'untagged merged release PRs' when multi-package config was introduced.

The web app had three separate HTTP client paths: orval React Query hooks (custom fetch mutator), a hand-written axios client for login/vault init, and bare functions in lib/api/ipfs.ts — none sharing token refresh logic.

The web app had duplicate orval code generation: packages/api-client (axios-functions mode for SDK consumers) and apps/web/src/api/ (react-query mode for the web app) — but the web app almost exclusively used the raw functions, not the hooks.
The API is intentionally zero-knowledge and imports no workspace crypto/core packages — it stores opaque blobs and the api-client package is generated from its OpenAPI spec to bridge consumers.
IPNS DHT publish via someguy sidecar was awaited despite being best-effort — the DB record is the authoritative source and resolveRecord() always prefers the DB cache.
Grafana Cloud free-tier instances hibernate and return HTTP 503 'Your instance is loading' on first deploy hit — transient, not a real failure.
CI verify step in .github/workflows/ci.yml still referenced apps/web/src/api/ after the directory was deleted in the consolidation refactor.

code.finding: result variable stays 'success' after fire-and-forget refactor — correct, since delegated routing is best-effort and the DB write is the authoritative publish.
createAxiosInstance() was not propagating new config options (withCredentials, refreshAccessToken) to the axios instance it created.
401 response interceptor with shared-promise deduplication for token refresh lives here; getCachedInstance() is a separate path intentionally without this interceptor (for SDK consumers).
headers.Authorization direct assignment is unsafe on AxiosHeaders objects — should use headers.set() or bracket notation.
logout, unlinkMethod, and deleteAccount all returned Promise<unknown> due to unsafe `as` casts — should use generated DTOs directly.
Download-with-progress path used raw fetch() bypassing the 401 interceptor; simplified to use axios ipfsControllerGet() with onDownloadProgress option, reducing file from 131 to 70 lines.
Web app had its own orval config generating react-query hooks into apps/web/src/api/ — 8812 lines of generated code, but hooks were only used for 1 endpoint (health check). Deleted entirely.

workflow: When release-please gets stuck with 'untagged merged release PRs', manually creating the tag/release with `gh release create` unblocks it for future runs.
fire-and-forget async operations in NestJS need a trailing .catch() to prevent unhandled promise rejections — bare detached promises will silently swallow errors.
Codecov patch coverage checks flag new lines added in review-comment fixes — test coverage must be added alongside the fix, not just for the original PR code.

When consolidating API clients, the orval `client:` mode (axios-functions vs react-query) is the key differentiator — switching consumers to raw function imports from the shared package then allows deleting the web-app-local generation entirely.
Using `chore` commit type does not trigger release-please version bumps — only `feat` and `fix` do. Build/CI fixes that block deployment should use `fix(ci)` to get a patch release.

friction: release-please was silently aborting tag creation due to missing `${component}` in title pattern — error message 'PR component: undefined does not match configured component' is not obvious without reading workflow logs carefully.
v0.25.1 tag had to be manually created because release-please was stuck, blocking the staging deployment workflow from being triggered.
Multiple rounds of automated reviewer comments (CodeRabbit + Copilot flagging the same missing .catch() independently) required separate reply-and-resolve steps per reviewer.
Codecov patch coverage failure appeared after review fixes were pushed, requiring a separate commit to add test coverage for the new error logging path.
CI workflow still referenced the deleted apps/web/src/api/ directory after the consolidation refactor, causing a verify step failure that required a hotfix commit.
Grafana Cloud free-tier hibernation caused a false deployment failure in the Tag Staging Release workflow, requiring a re-run of just that job.
open_items: PR #309 (refactor/consolidate-api-client) was still open at end of session — needs CI to pass and merging before staging can be tested with the unified token refresh.
Token refresh fix via the consolidated api-client (PR #309) has not been smoke-tested on staging — the original debugger-proposed fix was stashed/superseded by the refactor.
Tag Staging Release workflow still needs to be re-run successfully with v0.25.1 after PRs #308 and #309 are merged and a v0.25.2 patch release is cut if needed.
PR #307 (release-please title pattern fix) needs to be verified on the next release cycle to confirm release-please correctly matches component PRs going forward.
The someguy sidecar IPNS performance should be monitored on staging after the fire-and-forget fix to confirm publish latency is resolved — no staging verification occurred in this session.
